newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian credibility on line over Stet - Van Miert.
newsitem.headline: Italian credibility on line over Stet - Van Miert.

text.p: EU Commissioner Karel Van Miert was quoted as saying on Wednesday Italy's credibility was at stake over constant delays in plans to privatise state telecom group Stet and cut huge debts at state industrial holding IRI.
"There is a problem of credibility of political authority overall," Van Miert told Milan financial daily Il Sole 24 Ore in an interview from Strasburg.

The Italian government said on Monday it would merge Stet with its main operating arm Telecom Italia, remove them from IRI's books and place the combined entity under the wing of the Treasury in preparation for a sell-off in late 1997.

The government had previously said it was aiming to privatise Stet in the first quarter of 1997 but delays in parliamentary approval of legislation setting up a regulatory authority to police the industry had put this deadline in doubt.

Van Miert, who negotiated a 1993 agreement with the Italian government under which IRI was to cut its debts to below five trillion lire by the end of 1996, cast doubt on whether Italy would meet the new deadline.
"Who can guarantee to me that this time the privatisation will really be carried out?" said Van Miert.
IRI debts are expected to total some 23.5 trillion lire by the end of the year and the group is heading for losses in 1996 of up to three trillion lire.
"In Rome in September I was given guarantees that Stet would have been privatised by the spring of 1997 and instead, the other day, I had to note that it cannot be done before autumn."
Van Miert said the onus was now on the government to transfer Stet from IRI to the treasury and to forge ahead with its privatisation program.
